# Homelab My self-hosted homelab. I started it in December 2020 and it has grown one service at a time: media streaming and automation, a personal cloud, a local AI chat site, custom MCP servers, and a layer of self-healing watchdogs that keeps it all running without much hands-on work. This repo is a write-up, not a full config dump. The [watchdogs](watchdogs/) and the [example compose file](compose/) are real code from the server, cleaned up for publication. ## Hardware | Machine | Role | |---|---| | **Minisforum NAB6** mini PC (Intel i7-12650H) | Always-on server. Runs everything in Docker. | | **~48 TB mergerfs pool** (4 disks) | Media, documents, photos, ROMs, backups. | | **GPU workstation** (RTX 4070 Ti) | Off by default. Wakes over Wake-on-LAN when there's GPU work, then powers itself off when idle. | ## Services **Media** - Jellyfin for streaming, with Intel Quick Sync hardware transcoding. - Sonarr, Radarr, Prowlarr, Bazarr and Jellyseerr for automated acquisition, subtitles and requests. Quality profiles are managed as code with Recyclarr. - qBittorrent runs inside a Gluetun VPN container's network namespace. If the tunnel is down, the client has no network at all. - A separate music pipeline that turns playlists into a lossless FLAC library tagged with beets. - A small request widget injected into the Jellyfin UI, so users can request titles without leaving the player. **Personal cloud** - Nextcloud for files, calendar, contacts and photo sync, with face recognition. - RomM for a retro game library. - A Pterodactyl panel for hosting game servers. **Local AI** - LibreChat front end with Ollama models running on the GPU workstation. - A **wake-on-inference gateway**: the chat site stays up while the GPU box is off. When a request targets a local model, the gateway wakes the workstation, waits for it to boot, opens a tunnel, preloads the model, and then streams the response. A cold start takes about 45 seconds. When the queue goes idle, the workstation shuts itself down. - A self-hosted, sandboxed code interpreter and RAG over my own documents. **Custom MCP servers** (Model Context Protocol, so AI assistants can use the lab) - **Media**: one server covering Jellyfin, Sonarr, Radarr, Jellyseerr, Bazarr and the music pipeline. - **Nextcloud**: about 115 tools over WebDAV, OCS and CalDAV. - **Browser automation**: a hosted Playwright-based browser with per-conversation tab isolation and persistent sign-ins. - **An MCP router** that puts all of these behind two tools (`search_tools` and `call_tool`), using embedding search. Small local models can then work with hundreds of tools without filling their context. **Operations** - About 30 cron and systemd watchdogs that detect and heal specific failure modes (see [watchdogs/](watchdogs/)). - A foundation-level heartbeat that watches the watchdogs. - Nightly backups with restic to two separate disks, written directly to the disks rather than through the pool, with freshness markers that the heartbeat checks. - A userspace out-of-memory guard and per-container memory limits, added after the host locked up from memory pressure. ## Architecture ```mermaid flowchart LR users([Family devices]) --> proxy[Reverse proxy / tunnel] proxy --> jellyfin[Jellyfin] proxy --> nextcloud[Nextcloud] proxy --> chat[LibreChat] proxy --> mcp[MCP servers] subgraph server[Mini PC server] subgraph media[Media stack] jellyseerr[Jellyseerr] --> arr[Sonarr / Radarr] arr --> prowlarr[Prowlarr] arr --> qbit subgraph vpnns[VPN network namespace] gluetun[Gluetun VPN] --- qbit[qBittorrent] end arr --> jellyfin end nextcloud chat --> gateway[Wake-on-inference gateway] mcp --> router[MCP router] watchdogs[Watchdogs + heartbeat] -.heal.-> media backup[Nightly restic backups] end pool[(mergerfs pool ~48 TB)] media --> pool nextcloud --> pool backup --> disks[(Two backup disks)] gateway -- Wake-on-LAN + tunnel --> gpu[GPU workstation
Ollama] gluetun --> vpn((Commercial VPN)) ``` ## Lessons learned **1. "Running" isn't "working": the zombie VPN container.** The VPN container's WireGuard tunnel died, but the container stayed `running (unhealthy)`. Docker's restart policy only fires when a process exits, not when a health check fails, so nothing restarted it. Downloads were silently dead for about 36 hours. Three different watchdogs missed it, each in its own way: one read a cached exit-IP file that outlives the tunnel, one waited for self-recovery and never restarted anything, and one used `docker compose up -d`, which does nothing to a container that's already running. The fixes were a live egress test through the tunnel, a real restart, and a recreate of the client that shares the VPN's network namespace (its namespace reference goes stale after a restart). **2. Port forwarding can fail with every health check green.** The VPN's NAT-PMP renewal timed out, but the forwarded-port file still showed the old port. The torrent client went "firewalled", and downloads slowed to a trickle. Then my own stall manager made it worse: it marked each stalled release as failed, blocklisted it and searched again, and the next release stalled the same way. One episode went through seven releases in ten hours. Now a dedicated watchdog tests port reachability directly, and the stall manager won't act at all while the client is firewalled. **3. The slow downloads were a disk problem, not a network problem.** Total throughput was stuck around 1 MB/s with a healthy tunnel and plenty of peers. `iostat` showed the disks heavily busy with almost nothing being written: qBittorrent's disk I/O mode was set to *write-through*, so every small piece write was followed by an fsync. Switching to OS-cached writes raised throughput to about 50 MB/s. The API's integer values are also a trap: `0` isn't the default, it's `O_DIRECT`. **4. Pooled storage hides per-disk permissions.** After a new disk was added to the mergerfs pool, creating a top-level folder failed with `EACCES` even though the pool root was writable. mergerfs sends new files to the emptiest disk, and that disk's branch root was owned by root. A later version of the same bug was nastier: deletes failed for about a third of the files in one folder, seemingly at random. The files that failed all lived on the one disk whose copy of that subfolder had been recreated as root during a restore. Now I compare the same path across *every* branch instead of trusting what the pooled view shows. **5. My own automation deleted a whole download session.** A routine container recreate briefly broke the link between the *arr apps and the download client. Every torrent then looked orphaned, and over six hours my cleanup jobs removed more than 125 of them, some along with their data. The worst offender was a queue cleaner that had a "stuck for N minutes" setting but never actually used it. Fixes: a `keep` tag that every deletion path respects, a circuit breaker (if more than a few items look orphaned at once, it's a connection failure, so skip the run), and fail-safe behavior: if the client can't be reached, delete nothing. **6. One stale DNS setting, a dozen different errors.** An uninstalled mesh-VPN client left a global DNS override pointing at a resolver that only works from the host. Docker's embedded DNS copies the host's upstream servers when a container starts, so containers started after that point couldn't resolve anything. The symptoms looked unrelated: name-resolution errors, page-load timeouts, 60-second hangs, and a config tool failing with a confusing error about a color style. Every long-lived service now pins its DNS upstreams in compose. After any host DNS change, I check name resolution in every container, not only the ones that look broken. ## Repo layout ``` watchdogs/ representative self-healing scripts, plus a README on each compose/ a cleaned-up example of the core media stack ```

# Watchdogs

The homelab runs roughly 30 small cron/systemd watchdogs. Each one exists because a
specific failure happened at least once and nothing caught it. These four are
representative. They've been cleaned up for publication: hostnames, addresses,
paths and credentials all come from environment variables.

All of them follow the same rules:

- **Detect the real symptom, not a proxy for it.** Check that traffic actually
  flows, not that a status file exists.
- **Strike before you heal.** Most heals need two consecutive failures, so a
  transient blip or a normal reconnect window doesn't cause a restart.
- **Prefer the cheapest fix.** Sync a setting over the API before restarting a
  container; restart a container before touching the host.
- **Stay in your lane.** If a dependency is down, log it and defer to the watchdog
  that owns it.

| Script | Schedule | What it catches |
|---|---|---|
| [`server-heartbeat.sh`](server-heartbeat.sh) | systemd timer, every 2 min | The foundations every other watchdog assumes: LAN, internet, DNS, docker, cron, disk, memory, critical containers, backup freshness, and whether the *other* watchdogs are still logging. Heals only `systemd-resolved`, `cron`, and `docker`, and never host networking. It runs from systemd rather than cron so it still works when cron is dead. Has `--dry-run` and `--inject <scenario>` modes for a fault-injection test harness. |
| [`vpn-monitor.sh`](vpn-monitor.sh) | cron, every 5 min | VPN container that is "running" but not passing traffic. Does a live egress request through the tunnel, then a real restart, then recreates the torrent client that shares the VPN's network namespace. |
| [`port-forward-watchdog.sh`](port-forward-watchdog.sh) | cron, every 10 min | The VPN tunnel is up but the forwarded port silently died. Covers three cases: empty port (full heal), port drift between VPN and client (API sync only), and "firewalled" status (checks external reachability first, because NAT-PMP lease renewals cause false positives). |
| [`queue-gridlock-watchdog.sh`](queue-gridlock-watchdog.sh) | cron, every 5 min | Download slots filled with peerless torrents that will never start, or a corrupted DHT (`dht_nodes=0`) after repeated VPN flaps. Tracks its own "first seen stuck" time per torrent instead of trusting `added_on`, and never touches torrents tagged `keep`. |

## Notes

- **Log once.** If a script writes to its own log, cron must not *also* redirect
  stdout into that log, or every line appears twice.
- **State under `/tmp` is a trap for watchdogs that run as root.** With
  `fs.protected_regular=2`, even root can't write-open a file in sticky `/tmp`
  that another user owns. One stale user-owned strikes file silently disabled
  heal escalation for five weeks. Keep state in a directory each invoker owns
  (`/run/...`, `$XDG_RUNTIME_DIR`), and log loudly if a state write fails.
- **Deletion paths need circuit breakers.** If an automation suddenly sees every
  item as an orphan, the problem is almost always a broken connection, not real
  orphans. Skip that run and leave the items alone.

# Example: the core of the media stack, cleaned up for publication.
# All values come from a .env file next to this one (see .env.example).
# The torrent client shares the VPN container's network namespace, so every
# byte it sends goes through the tunnel or nowhere.

services:
  gluetun:
    image: qmcgaw/gluetun:${GLUETUN_TAG}
    container_name: gluetun
    cap_add: [NET_ADMIN]
    devices: [/dev/net/tun:/dev/net/tun]
    environment:
      - VPN_SERVICE_PROVIDER=${VPN_PROVIDER}
      - VPN_TYPE=wireguard
      - WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY=${WIREGUARD_PRIVATE_KEY}
      - SERVER_COUNTRIES=${VPN_SERVER_COUNTRIES}
      - VPN_PORT_FORWARDING=on
      - TZ=${TZ}
    ports:
      - "${QBIT_WEBUI_BIND}:${QBIT_WEBUI_PORT}:${QBIT_WEBUI_PORT}"   # bind to loopback only
    restart: unless-stopped

  qbittorrent:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/qbittorrent:${QBIT_TAG}
    container_name: qbittorrent
    network_mode: "service:gluetun"     # no VPN, no network
    depends_on:
      gluetun:
        condition: service_healthy
    environment:
      - PUID=${PUID}
      - PGID=${PGID}
      - TZ=${TZ}
      - WEBUI_PORT=${QBIT_WEBUI_PORT}
    volumes:
      - ${CONFIG_ROOT}/qbittorrent:/config
      - ${DOWNLOADS_ROOT}:/downloads
    restart: unless-stopped

  sonarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/sonarr:${SONARR_TAG}
    container_name: sonarr
    dns: ["${DNS_PRIMARY}", "${DNS_SECONDARY}"]   # pin upstreams; see README lessons
    environment: [PUID=${PUID}, PGID=${PGID}, TZ=${TZ}]
    volumes:
      - ${CONFIG_ROOT}/sonarr:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT}:/media
      - ${DOWNLOADS_ROOT}:/downloads
    restart: unless-stopped

  radarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/radarr:${RADARR_TAG}
    container_name: radarr
    dns: ["${DNS_PRIMARY}", "${DNS_SECONDARY}"]
    environment: [PUID=${PUID}, PGID=${PGID}, TZ=${TZ}]
    volumes:
      - ${CONFIG_ROOT}/radarr:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT}:/media
      - ${DOWNLOADS_ROOT}:/downloads
    restart: unless-stopped

  prowlarr:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/prowlarr:${PROWLARR_TAG}
    container_name: prowlarr
    dns: ["${DNS_PRIMARY}", "${DNS_SECONDARY}"]
    environment: [PUID=${PUID}, PGID=${PGID}, TZ=${TZ}]
    volumes:
      - ${CONFIG_ROOT}/prowlarr:/config
    restart: unless-stopped

  jellyfin:
    image: lscr.io/linuxserver/jellyfin:${JELLYFIN_TAG}
    container_name: jellyfin
    devices: [/dev/dri:/dev/dri]        # Intel Quick Sync hardware transcoding
    environment: [PUID=${PUID}, PGID=${PGID}, TZ=${TZ}]
    volumes:
      - ${CONFIG_ROOT}/jellyfin:/config
      - ${MEDIA_ROOT}:/media:ro
    restart: unless-stopped

#!/bin/bash
# port-forward-watchdog.sh — defends the torrent client's port-forwarding pipeline.
# Runs every 10 minutes from cron. Three failure modes covered:
#
#   A. EMPTY/STALE PORT — the VPN container's NAT-PMP request fails and its
#      forwarded_port file is empty or "0". The client can't accept incoming
#      peers. Heal: restart the VPN container + recreate the client.
#
#   B. PORT DRIFT — the VPN container has a port but the client's listen_port
#      doesn't match it (typical after a VPN restart without a client recreate).
#      Heal: sync via the client's API, no container restart needed.
#
#   C. FIREWALLED — ports match, but the client reports connection_status=firewalled.
#      Before healing, an external reachability check is performed. If the port IS
#      reachable, "firewalled" is a false positive from a NAT-PMP lease renewal, so
#      we only reannounce. Restart only if the port is genuinely unreachable.
#
# A and C use a 2-strike threshold (one cron interval apart) to avoid acting during
# the normal post-restart negotiation window. B fires immediately (cheap API call).
#
# Required environment (e.g. from an .env file sourced by the cron wrapper):
#   COMPOSE_DIR, QBIT_URL, QBIT_USER, QBIT_PASS
# Optional: VPN_CONTAINER, QBIT_CONTAINER, PORTCHECK_URL, LOG_FILE, STATE_DIR

set -u
: "${COMPOSE_DIR:?set COMPOSE_DIR}"
: "${QBIT_URL:?set QBIT_URL (e.g. http://localhost:<webui-port>)}"
: "${QBIT_USER:?set QBIT_USER}"
: "${QBIT_PASS:?set QBIT_PASS}"
VPN_CONTAINER="${VPN_CONTAINER:-gluetun}"
QBIT_CONTAINER="${QBIT_CONTAINER:-qbittorrent}"
PORTCHECK_URL="${PORTCHECK_URL:-}"   # optional external port-check API
LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-$COMPOSE_DIR/logs/port-forward-watchdog.log}"
STATE_DIR="${STATE_DIR:-${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/port-forward-watchdog}"
STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/strikes"
SESSION_JAR="$STATE_DIR/qbit-session"
CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_THRESHOLD=2

mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")"
log() { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $*" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }

qbit_login() {
    curl -s -c "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/auth/login" \
        --data-urlencode "username=$QBIT_USER" --data-urlencode "password=$QBIT_PASS" \
        -o /dev/null 2>&1
}

json_field() {  # json_field <key> <default>
    python3 -c 'import sys,json
try: print(json.load(sys.stdin)[sys.argv[1]])
except Exception: print(sys.argv[2])' "$1" "$2" 2>/dev/null
}

get_conn_status()      { curl -s -b "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/transfer/info"   | json_field connection_status unknown; }
get_qbit_listen_port() { curl -s -b "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/app/preferences" | json_field listen_port 0; }
get_vpn_port()         { docker exec "$VPN_CONTAINER" cat /tmp/gluetun/forwarded_port 2>/dev/null; }

set_qbit_listen_port() {
    local payload="{\"listen_port\": $1, \"random_port\": false, \"upnp\": false}"
    curl -s -b "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/app/setPreferences" \
        --data-urlencode "json=$payload" -o /dev/null 2>&1
}

reannounce_all() {
    curl -s -b "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/torrents/reannounce" \
        --data "hashes=all" -o /dev/null 2>&1
}

# Returns 0 if port $1 is reachable on the VPN exit address, 1 otherwise.
# Without a configured checker we can't prove reachability, so assume unreachable.
port_reachable_externally() {
    [ -z "$PORTCHECK_URL" ] && return 1
    local port=$1 exit_ip result
    exit_ip=$(docker exec "$VPN_CONTAINER" cat /tmp/gluetun/ip 2>/dev/null)
    [ -z "$exit_ip" ] && return 1
    result=$(curl -s --max-time 8 "$PORTCHECK_URL" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "{\"host\":\"$exit_ip\",\"ports\":[$port]}" 2>/dev/null | \
        python3 -c "import json,sys
try:
    d=json.load(sys.stdin)
    print('yes' if d.get('check',[{}])[0].get('status') else 'no')
except Exception: print('no')" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$result" = "yes" ]
}

heal_full() {
    local reason=$1
    log "HEAL ($reason): restart $VPN_CONTAINER + force-recreate $QBIT_CONTAINER"
    (cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose restart "$VPN_CONTAINER" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1)
    # Wait up to 90s for the VPN container to obtain a forwarded port
    local waited=0 p
    while [ $waited -lt 90 ]; do
        sleep 5; waited=$((waited+5))
        p=$(get_vpn_port)
        if [ -n "$p" ] && [ "$p" != "0" ]; then
            log "  VPN acquired a forwarded port after ${waited}s"; break
        fi
    done
    # The client shares the VPN container's network namespace; after a VPN restart
    # its netns reference is stale, so it must be recreated, not just restarted.
    (cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose up -d --force-recreate "$QBIT_CONTAINER" >> "$LOG_FILE" 2>&1)
    sleep 15
    qbit_login
    local new_fp
    new_fp=$(get_vpn_port)
    if [ -n "$new_fp" ] && [ "$new_fp" != "0" ]; then
        set_qbit_listen_port "$new_fp"
        sleep 2
        reannounce_all
        log "  synced client listen_port to the new forwarded port"
    fi
    log "HEAL done. status=$(get_conn_status)"
}

# ---- main ----

running=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}')
grep -qx "$VPN_CONTAINER"  <<<"$running" || { log "$VPN_CONTAINER not running; deferring to VPN watchdog"; exit 0; }
grep -qx "$QBIT_CONTAINER" <<<"$running" || { log "$QBIT_CONTAINER not running; deferring to client watchdog"; exit 0; }

FP=$(get_vpn_port)
PREV=$(cat "$STATE_FILE" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
qbit_login
LP=$(get_qbit_listen_port)
STATUS=$(get_conn_status)

# --- A. Empty/0 forwarded port ---
if [ -z "$FP" ] || [ "$FP" = "0" ]; then
    NEW=$((PREV + 1)); echo "$NEW" > "$STATE_FILE"
    log "no forwarded port (strike $NEW/$CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_THRESHOLD), status=$STATUS"
    if [ "$NEW" -ge "$CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_THRESHOLD" ]; then
        heal_full "empty-port"; echo 0 > "$STATE_FILE"
    fi
    exit 0
fi

# --- B. Port drift (cheap fix, no restart) ---
if [ -n "$LP" ] && [ "$LP" != "0" ] && [ "$LP" != "$FP" ]; then
    log "PORT DRIFT: VPN port != client listen_port — syncing via API"
    set_qbit_listen_port "$FP"
    sleep 2
    reannounce_all
fi

# --- C. Firewalled despite a valid port ---
if [ "$STATUS" = "firewalled" ]; then
    NEW=$((PREV + 1)); echo "$NEW" > "$STATE_FILE"
    log "firewalled (strike $NEW/$CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_THRESHOLD)"
    if [ "$NEW" -ge "$CONSECUTIVE_FAIL_THRESHOLD" ]; then
        if port_reachable_externally "$FP"; then
            log "  port is externally reachable — false positive (lease renewal). reannouncing only."
            reannounce_all
        else
            log "  port confirmed unreachable — proceeding with heal."
            heal_full "firewalled"
        fi
        echo 0 > "$STATE_FILE"
    fi
    exit 0
fi

# Healthy
[ "$PREV" -gt 0 ] && log "recovered: status=$STATUS"
echo 0 > "$STATE_FILE"

#!/bin/bash
# queue-gridlock-watchdog.sh
# Detects torrent-client gridlock: ~0 download speed with active slots full of
# stuck/peerless torrents, or DHT subsystem corruption (dht_nodes=0, seen after
# repeated VPN flaps). Removes stuck items so the *arr apps can re-search, and
# restarts the client on sustained DHT failure. Runs every 5 minutes from cron.
#
# Required environment: QBIT_URL, QBIT_USER, QBIT_PASS
# Optional: QBIT_CONTAINER, PROTECTED_TAG, LOG_FILE, STATE_DIR

set -u
: "${QBIT_URL:?set QBIT_URL (e.g. http://localhost:<webui-port>)}"
: "${QBIT_USER:?set QBIT_USER}"
: "${QBIT_PASS:?set QBIT_PASS}"
QBIT_CONTAINER="${QBIT_CONTAINER:-qbittorrent}"
PROTECTED_TAG="${PROTECTED_TAG:-keep}"   # manually curated torrents are never deleted
STATE="${STATE_DIR:-${XDG_RUNTIME_DIR:-/tmp}/queue-gridlock}"
LOG="${LOG_FILE:-$STATE/queue-gridlock-watchdog.log}"
SESSION_JAR="$STATE/qbit-session"

# Thresholds
ZERO_DL_MINUTES=15            # sustained ~0 dl speed -> intervention
DHT_FAIL_MINUTES=5            # sustained dht=0 -> client restart
METADL_AGE_MINUTES=20         # metaDL with 0 peers stuck this long -> delete
STALLED_AGE_MINUTES=60        # stalledDL at 0% with 0 peers stuck this long -> delete

mkdir -p "$STATE" "$(dirname "$LOG")"
ts()  { date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; }
log() { echo "[$(ts)] $*" >> "$LOG"; }   # cron must NOT also redirect into $LOG (double lines)
api() { curl -s -b "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/$1" "${@:2}"; }

# Auth
AUTH=$(curl -s -c "$SESSION_JAR" "$QBIT_URL/api/v2/auth/login" \
  --data-urlencode "username=$QBIT_USER" --data-urlencode "password=$QBIT_PASS")
[ "$AUTH" = "Ok." ] || { log "ERROR: client auth failed"; exit 1; }

XFER=$(api transfer/info)
[ -n "$XFER" ] || { log "ERROR: no transfer info"; exit 1; }

DL_SPEED=$(echo "$XFER" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['dl_info_speed'])")
DHT=$(echo "$XFER" | python3 -c "import json,sys; print(json.load(sys.stdin)['dht_nodes'])")

NOW=$(date +%s)
[ -f "$STATE/zero_dl_since" ]  || echo 0 > "$STATE/zero_dl_since"
[ -f "$STATE/dht_zero_since" ] || echo 0 > "$STATE/dht_zero_since"
ZERO_SINCE=$(cat "$STATE/zero_dl_since")
DHT_SINCE=$(cat "$STATE/dht_zero_since")

# --- DHT tracking ---
if [ "$DHT" = "0" ]; then
  [ "$DHT_SINCE" = "0" ] && echo "$NOW" > "$STATE/dht_zero_since" && DHT_SINCE=$NOW
  AGE=$((NOW - DHT_SINCE))
  if [ $AGE -ge $((DHT_FAIL_MINUTES * 60)) ]; then
    log "ALERT: DHT down for ${AGE}s — restarting $QBIT_CONTAINER"
    docker restart "$QBIT_CONTAINER" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    echo 0 > "$STATE/dht_zero_since"
    exit 0
  fi
else
  echo 0 > "$STATE/dht_zero_since"
fi

# --- Active-slot gridlock detection ---
TORRENTS_FILE="$STATE/torrents.json"
api torrents/info > "$TORRENTS_FILE"
STUCK_DB="$STATE/stuck-since.json"      # {hash: first-epoch-seen-stuck}

# Track how long each torrent has been *continuously* stuck. added_on can't be trusted
# (a torrent may sit queued for days before starting), so we keep our own first-seen
# timestamp and only delete once it has been stuck past the threshold.
DELETED=$(METADL_AGE=$((METADL_AGE_MINUTES * 60)) STALLED_AGE=$((STALLED_AGE_MINUTES * 60)) \
  NOW=$NOW TFILE=$TORRENTS_FILE DB=$STUCK_DB TAG=$PROTECTED_TAG python3 <<'PY'
import json, os
t = json.load(open(os.environ['TFILE']))
now = int(os.environ['NOW'])
metadl_age = int(os.environ['METADL_AGE'])
stalled_age = int(os.environ['STALLED_AGE'])
tag = os.environ['TAG']
dbp = os.environ['DB']
try: db = json.load(open(dbp))
except Exception: db = {}
new_db, to_del = {}, []
for x in t:
    h = x['hash']
    if tag in [s.strip() for s in x.get('tags', '').split(',')]:
        continue                          # protected: never delete
    peers = x.get('num_seeds', 0) + x.get('num_leechs', 0)
    is_metadl  = x['state'] == 'metaDL' and peers == 0
    is_stalled = x['state'] == 'stalledDL' and x['progress'] < 0.001 and peers == 0
    if not (is_metadl or is_stalled):
        continue                          # not stuck now -> dropped from db (timer resets)
    since = db.get(h, now)
    new_db[h] = since
    if now - since >= (metadl_age if is_metadl else stalled_age):
        to_del.append(h)
json.dump(new_db, open(dbp, 'w'))
print('|'.join(to_del))
PY
)

if [ -n "$DELETED" ]; then
  CNT=$(echo "$DELETED" | tr '|' '\n' | wc -l)
  log "Deleting $CNT stuck (0-peer, 0% progress) torrents"
  api torrents/delete --data-urlencode "hashes=$DELETED" --data "deleteFiles=true" -o /dev/null
fi

# --- Zero-throughput gridlock: only flag with work queued but no bytes moving ---
ACTIVE_OR_QUEUED=$(TFILE=$TORRENTS_FILE python3 -c "
import json, os
t = json.load(open(os.environ['TFILE']))
print(sum(1 for x in t if x['state'] in ('downloading','metaDL','stalledDL','queuedDL','forcedDL','allocating','checkingDL')))")

if [ "$DL_SPEED" -lt 1024 ] && [ "$ACTIVE_OR_QUEUED" -gt 0 ]; then
  [ "$ZERO_SINCE" = "0" ] && echo "$NOW" > "$STATE/zero_dl_since" && ZERO_SINCE=$NOW
  AGE=$((NOW - ZERO_SINCE))
  if [ $AGE -ge $((ZERO_DL_MINUTES * 60)) ]; then
    log "ALERT: ~0 dl speed for ${AGE}s with $ACTIVE_OR_QUEUED active/queued torrents"
    if [ "$DHT" -gt 50 ]; then
      log "DHT ok ($DHT nodes): reannounce + start all"
      api torrents/reannounce --data "hashes=all" -o /dev/null
      api torrents/start      --data "hashes=all" -o /dev/null
    else
      log "DHT degraded ($DHT nodes): restarting $QBIT_CONTAINER"
      docker restart "$QBIT_CONTAINER" >> "$LOG" 2>&1
    fi
    echo 0 > "$STATE/zero_dl_since"
  fi
else
  echo 0 > "$STATE/zero_dl_since"
fi

log "tick: dl=$((DL_SPEED/1024))KB/s dht=$DHT active_or_queued=$ACTIVE_OR_QUEUED"

#!/bin/bash
# server-heartbeat.sh — foundation-level meta-watchdog.
#
# Every per-service watchdog assumes the foundations work. If cron, docker, DNS,
# or a disk dies, they all go silent at once. This script watches the foundations:
# LAN, internet, DNS, docker, cron, disk, memory, peer-watchdog liveness, critical
# containers, and backup freshness. It conservatively heals systemd-resolved, cron,
# and docker after a 2-strike threshold. Host networking is never auto-restarted
# (that could lock out remote access).
#
# Runs from a systemd timer every 2 minutes — NOT cron, since cron is one of the
# things it checks.
#
# Outputs: structured log + JSON state file + a beacon file touched on all-green.
# Modes: --dry-run (log heals, don't execute), --inject <scenario> (synthetic
# failure injection, used by the test harness without disconnecting anything).
#
# Configuration (all via environment, e.g. an EnvironmentFile= in the unit):
#   SH_LAN_GATEWAY        required: address of the LAN gateway to ping
#   SH_INTERNET_PROBES    required: space-separated public hosts to ping
#   SH_DNS_PROBES         names to resolve (default: example.com example.org)
#   SH_CRITICAL_CONTAINERS space-separated container names
#   SH_PEER_WATCHDOG_LOGS space-separated log files of watchdogs that log every run
#   SH_DISK_MOUNTS        mounts to check for >=90% usage (default: / /home)
#   SH_BACKUP_MARKERS     space-separated .last_success files written by backups
#   SH_STATE_DIR, SH_LOG_FILE, SH_HEAL_THRESHOLD, SH_WATCHDOG_STALE_SECS,
#   SH_BACKUP_STALE_DAYS

set -u

# ---- config ----
STATE_DIR="${SH_STATE_DIR:-/run/server-heartbeat}"   # root-owned; see README on /tmp
LOG_FILE="${SH_LOG_FILE:-/var/log/server-heartbeat.log}"
STATE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/state.json"
STRIKE_FILE="$STATE_DIR/strikes"
BEACON_FILE="$STATE_DIR/beacon"
HEAL_THRESHOLD="${SH_HEAL_THRESHOLD:-2}"
LAN_GATEWAY="${SH_LAN_GATEWAY:-}"
read -r -a INTERNET_PROBES <<<"${SH_INTERNET_PROBES:-}"
read -r -a DNS_PROBES <<<"${SH_DNS_PROBES:-example.com example.org}"
WATCHDOG_STALE_SECS="${SH_WATCHDOG_STALE_SECS:-1800}"  # 30 min
read -r -a CRITICAL_CONTAINERS <<<"${SH_CRITICAL_CONTAINERS:-gluetun qbittorrent jellyfin nextcloud}"
# Only watchdogs that log on EVERY run belong here: incident-only loggers are
# silent when healthy, so their silence is not a liveness signal.
read -r -a PEER_WATCHDOG_LOGS <<<"${SH_PEER_WATCHDOG_LOGS:-}"
read -r -a DISK_MOUNTS <<<"${SH_DISK_MOUNTS:-/ /home}"
# Backups write a marker only when a run fully succeeds. Check every copy, because
# a mirror-copy failure is exactly the kind of half-failure that hides.
read -r -a BACKUP_MARKERS <<<"${SH_BACKUP_MARKERS:-}"
BACKUP_STALE_DAYS="${SH_BACKUP_STALE_DAYS:-2}"

# ---- args ----
DRY_RUN=0
INJECT=""
while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --dry-run) DRY_RUN=1 ;;
    --inject) INJECT="${2:-}"; shift ;;
    -h|--help)
      cat <<EOF
Usage: $(basename "$0") [--dry-run] [--inject SCENARIO]
  --dry-run     Run real checks, log heal actions instead of executing them.
  --inject SCN  Force a check to fail without touching reality. Scenarios:
                  lan_down internet_down dns_broken docker_dead cron_dead
                  watchdog_stale disk_full mem_high container_missing backup_stale
EOF
      exit 0 ;;
    *) echo "unknown arg: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
  shift
done

mkdir -p "$STATE_DIR" "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")"
ts()  { date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'; }
log() { echo "[$(ts)] $*" >>"$LOG_FILE"; }

# ---- strike persistence ----
declare -A STRIKES=( [dns]=0 [docker]=0 [cron]=0 )
load_strikes() {
  [[ -f "$STRIKE_FILE" ]] || return 0
  while IFS='=' read -r k v; do
    [[ -z "$k" || "$k" == \#* ]] && continue
    STRIKES[$k]=$v
  done <"$STRIKE_FILE"
}
save_strikes() {
  if ! : >"$STRIKE_FILE" 2>/dev/null; then
    # A silent failure here means the 2-strike heal can never fire. Be loud.
    log "ERROR: cannot write $STRIKE_FILE — heal escalation disabled"; return 1
  fi
  for k in "${!STRIKES[@]}"; do echo "$k=${STRIKES[$k]}" >>"$STRIKE_FILE"; done
}

# ---- checks: each prints "PASS|FAIL|SKIP detail" and returns 0 on pass ----

check_lan() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == lan_down ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  [[ -z "$LAN_GATEWAY" ]] && { echo "SKIP SH_LAN_GATEWAY unset"; return 0; }
  local i
  for i in 1 2 3; do
    ping -c 1 -W 2 "$LAN_GATEWAY" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  done
  echo "FAIL gateway unreachable"; return 1
}

check_internet() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == internet_down ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  (( ${#INTERNET_PROBES[@]} )) || { echo "SKIP SH_INTERNET_PROBES unset"; return 0; }
  local h
  for h in "${INTERNET_PROBES[@]}"; do
    ping -c 1 -W 2 "$h" >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  done
  echo "FAIL no internet probes reachable"; return 1
}

check_dns() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == dns_broken ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  local n
  for n in "${DNS_PROBES[@]}"; do
    getent hosts "$n" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "FAIL cannot resolve $n"; return 1; }
  done
  echo "PASS"; return 0
}

check_docker() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == docker_dead ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  timeout 10 docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL docker daemon unreachable"; return 1
}

check_cron() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == cron_dead ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  systemctl is-active --quiet cron && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL cron not active"; return 1
}

check_watchdog_liveness() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == watchdog_stale ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  local now stale=() f mt
  now=$(date +%s)
  for f in "${PEER_WATCHDOG_LOGS[@]}"; do
    [[ -f "$f" ]] || { stale+=("$(basename "$f"):missing"); continue; }
    mt=$(stat -c %Y "$f" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    (( now - mt > WATCHDOG_STALE_SECS )) && stale+=("$(basename "$f"):$(( (now - mt) / 60 ))m")
  done
  (( ${#stale[@]} == 0 )) && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL stale: ${stale[*]}"; return 1
}

check_disk() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == disk_full ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  local low=() used mount
  while read -r used mount; do
    used=${used%\%}
    [[ "$used" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]] && (( used >= 90 )) && low+=("$mount=${used}%")
  done < <(df --output=pcent,target "${DISK_MOUNTS[@]}" 2>/dev/null | tail -n +2)
  (( ${#low[@]} == 0 )) && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL ${low[*]}"; return 1
}

check_memory() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == mem_high ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  local total used swt swu pct
  read -r total used <<<"$(free -m | awk '/^Mem:/{print $2, $3}')"
  read -r swt swu   <<<"$(free -m | awk '/^Swap:/{print $2, $3}')"
  pct=$(( (used + swu) * 100 / (total + swt + 1) ))
  (( pct < 90 )) && { echo "PASS mem+swap=${pct}%"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL mem+swap=${pct}%"; return 1
}

check_containers() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == container_missing ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  timeout 10 docker info >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "SKIP docker unreachable"; return 0; }
  local missing=() c running
  running=$(docker ps --format '{{.Names}}' 2>/dev/null)
  for c in "${CRITICAL_CONTAINERS[@]}"; do
    grep -qx "$c" <<<"$running" || missing+=("$c")
  done
  (( ${#missing[@]} == 0 )) && { echo "PASS"; return 0; }
  echo "FAIL missing: ${missing[*]}"; return 1
}

check_backup() {
  [[ "$INJECT" == backup_stale ]] && { echo "FAIL injected"; return 1; }
  (( ${#BACKUP_MARKERS[@]} )) || { echo "SKIP no backup markers configured"; return 0; }
  local now mt marker oldest=-1 missing=()
  now=$(date +%s)
  for marker in "${BACKUP_MARKERS[@]}"; do
    [[ -f "$marker" ]] || { missing+=("$marker"); continue; }
    mt=$(stat -c %Y "$marker" 2>/dev/null || echo 0)
    (( oldest < 0 || mt < oldest )) && oldest=$mt
  done
  (( ${#missing[@]} )) && { echo "FAIL no backup marker: ${missing[*]}"; return 1; }
  if (( now - oldest > BACKUP_STALE_DAYS * 86400 )); then
    echo "FAIL last backup $(( (now - oldest) / 86400 ))d ago"; return 1
  fi
  echo "PASS $(( (now - oldest) / 86400 ))d ago"; return 0
}

# ---- heal ----
do_heal() {
  local target="$1"
  if (( DRY_RUN )); then log "DRY-RUN would heal: $target"; return 0; fi
  case "$target" in
    systemd-resolved|cron|docker)
      if systemctl restart "$target" 2>>"$LOG_FILE"; then
        log "HEAL executed: systemctl restart $target"; return 0
      fi
      log "HEAL FAILED: systemctl restart $target"; return 1 ;;
    *) log "unknown heal target: $target"; return 1 ;;
  esac
}

# ---- main ----
main() {
  load_strikes
  declare -A RESULTS
  local checks=(lan internet dns docker cron watchdog_liveness disk memory containers backup)
  local chk out
  for chk in "${checks[@]}"; do
    out=$("check_$chk")
    RESULTS[$chk]="$out"
    log "check_$chk: $out"
  done

  # strike-and-heal for the three healable checks
  local healed=() target
  for chk in dns docker cron; do
    if [[ "${RESULTS[$chk]}" == FAIL* ]]; then
      STRIKES[$chk]=$(( STRIKES[$chk] + 1 ))
      log "strike $chk=${STRIKES[$chk]}/$HEAL_THRESHOLD"
      if (( STRIKES[$chk] >= HEAL_THRESHOLD )); then
        target="$chk"; [[ "$chk" == dns ]] && target="systemd-resolved"
        do_heal "$target" && { healed+=("$target"); STRIKES[$chk]=0; }
      fi
    else
      STRIKES[$chk]=0
    fi
  done
  save_strikes

  # JSON state
  local json_checks="{}" status reason
  for chk in "${checks[@]}"; do
    case "${RESULTS[$chk]}" in PASS*) status=pass ;; SKIP*) status=skip ;; *) status=fail ;; esac
    reason="${RESULTS[$chk]#* }"
    json_checks=$(jq --arg k "$chk" --arg s "$status" --arg r "$reason" \
      '. + {($k): {status: $s, detail: $r}}' <<<"$json_checks")
  done
  local healed_json="[]"
  (( ${#healed[@]} )) && healed_json=$(printf '%s\n' "${healed[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)

  jq -n --arg ts "$(ts)" --argjson dry "$DRY_RUN" --arg inject "$INJECT" \
    --argjson checks "$json_checks" --argjson healed "$healed_json" \
    --argjson strikes "$(jq -n --argjson d "${STRIKES[dns]}" --argjson dk "${STRIKES[docker]}" --argjson c "${STRIKES[cron]}" '{dns:$d, docker:$dk, cron:$c}')" \
    '{ts:$ts, dry_run:($dry==1), inject:$inject, checks:$checks, strikes:$strikes, healed:$healed}' \
    >"$STATE_FILE"

  # beacon: touched only when no check failed
  local all_ok=1
  for chk in "${checks[@]}"; do [[ "${RESULTS[$chk]}" == FAIL* ]] && all_ok=0; done
  (( all_ok )) && touch "$BEACON_FILE" 2>/dev/null
  return 0
}

main

#!/bin/bash
# vpn-monitor.sh — verifies the VPN container actually carries traffic, and
# recovers it when it doesn't. Runs every 5 minutes from cron.
#
# The earlier version of this script read the VPN container's cached exit-IP file
# and reported "healthy" for an entire 36-hour outage: the file survives a dead
# tunnel. It also "restarted" with `docker compose up -d`, which is a no-op for a
# container that is still running. This version does a live egress test and a
# real restart, then recreates the namespace-sharing client.
#
# Required environment: COMPOSE_DIR, EGRESS_CHECK_URL
# Optional: VPN_CONTAINER, QBIT_CONTAINER, LOG_FILE

set -u
: "${COMPOSE_DIR:?set COMPOSE_DIR}"
VPN_CONTAINER="${VPN_CONTAINER:-gluetun}"
QBIT_CONTAINER="${QBIT_CONTAINER:-qbittorrent}"
EGRESS_CHECK_URL="${EGRESS_CHECK_URL:?set EGRESS_CHECK_URL (any what-is-my-IP endpoint)}"
LOG_FILE="${LOG_FILE:-$COMPOSE_DIR/logs/vpn-monitor.log}"
MAX_LOG_SIZE=10485760  # 10MB

mkdir -p "$(dirname "$LOG_FILE")"
log() { echo "[$(date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')] $1" >> "$LOG_FILE"; }

rotate_log() {
    if [ -f "$LOG_FILE" ] && [ "$(stat -c%s "$LOG_FILE")" -gt $MAX_LOG_SIZE ]; then
        mv "$LOG_FILE" "${LOG_FILE}.old"
    fi
}

# Live check: container health AND an actual request through the tunnel right now.
check_vpn() {
    local health
    health=$(docker inspect --format='{{.State.Health.Status}}' "$VPN_CONTAINER" 2>/dev/null)
    [ "$health" = "healthy" ] || return 1
    docker exec "$VPN_CONTAINER" sh -c "wget -qO- --timeout=8 '$EGRESS_CHECK_URL'" >/dev/null 2>&1
}

restart_containers() {
    log "VPN check failed — force-restarting $VPN_CONTAINER"
    (cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose restart "$VPN_CONTAINER")
    sleep 30
    if check_vpn; then
        # The client uses network_mode: service:<vpn>; its netns reference is now stale.
        (cd "$COMPOSE_DIR" && docker compose up -d --force-recreate "$QBIT_CONTAINER")
        log "VPN reconnected; $QBIT_CONTAINER recreated against the fresh VPN container"
    else
        log "ERROR: VPN failed to reconnect after restart"
    fi
}

rotate_log
if check_vpn; then
    log "VPN is connected and passing traffic"
else
    log "WARNING: VPN is not passing traffic"
    restart_containers
fi
